newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Drought-affected Queensland has recent rains.
newsitem.headline: Drought-affected Queensland has recent rains.

text.p: Widespread rainfall was recorded across much of central, western and southern Queensland during the past month, Queensland's Department of Primary Industries said in its latest drought situation report.
Falls were patchy but generally totals above 25 millimetres proved beneficial to warm conditions that prevailed across much of the state.

Drought affected areas in central Queensland and in coastal areas north of Brisbane were not sufficient to alleviate drought conditions. Useful falls in the far southwest should generate winter herbage and provide a bonus for graziers in these areas, it said.
Climate forecasts suggest that the chance of average rainfall during the June-August period range from 10 percent to 30 percent over most of southern and central Queensland, it said.

Persistent strongly negative Southern Oscillation Index (SOI) values, and the continued deterioration in sea-surface temperature patterns in the Pacific Ocean indicate a high probability of below average rainfall in many districts of eastern Australia for the remainder of 1997, it said.
An El Nino has now developed in the Pacific Ocean, it said.
The consistently negative SOI phase during April-May indicated a higher probability than normal of late-season frost in some areas, it said.
The chances of severe frosts were greater in southern and inland regions of Queensland and northern inland districts of New South Wales, it said.
